attempts.summary: Set up nginx on node1 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 using certificates issued by a local CA and short-lived by design (5 min validity) so renewal is observable. A systemd timer (cert-renew.timer, every 30s) runs /usr/local/sbin/cert-renew.sh, which uses openssl x509 -checkend to detect certs within 180s of expiry, reissues via openssl ca, atomically replaces the fullchain, and runs `nginx -s reload` (graceful, connection-preserving). Verified two live automatic renewals occurred (serial 1000->1001->1002) while continuous curl polling against https://$NODE_IP:8443/ returned HTTP 200 with zero failures throughout, including the exact second of the cert swap. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, rebooted node1 via `reboot`, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified nginx, cert-renew.timer, the on-disk cert/CA state, and HTTPS all recovered post-reboot with no data loss (timer and nginx both enabled, survived reboot, resumed on schedule).
